narratives.name: Multiplying RHEL Pipeline Through Distributor Channel Leverage
narratives.description: How a structured distributor campaign transforms hidden free Linux workloads into measurable RHEL pipeline through a two-tier cascade model, provocation-based conversation starters, and signal-matched sales plays.

narrativeContexts.context: The RHEL Campaign practice recognizes that thousands of free and community Linux workloads across enterprise estates represent invisible pipeline -- servers running CentOS, Oracle Linux, AlmaLinux, and Rocky Linux that never appear in forecasts or opportunity trackers. Designing the campaign requires mapping the complete channel cascade from Red Hat through distributors to resellers to end customers, identifying the multiplication mathematics that make one distributor activation produce twenty-five or more customer conversations, and selecting the provocative evidence-based hooks that open doors without pushing products. The design phase establishes four signal-matched sales plays (CentOS Stranded, Commercial Linux Renewer, Modernization Buyer, Extend Support) and three conversation starters (Security/CVE, Post-Quantum Cryptography, AI Foundation) as the campaign's core intellectual property.

Building the campaign infrastructure requires simultaneously investing in three pillars: enablement that equips resellers with conversation capability rather than product knowledge, marketing that generates demand through co-branded assets and MDF-funded events, and incentives that make the economic mathematics work for every tier of the cascade through deal registration rebates and co-sell Solution Architect support. The half-day RHEL sales bootcamp, TCO/ROI calculator, qualification framework, and conversation starter kits are built and tested with wave-one resellers before broader deployment.

Campaign execution follows a disciplined four-phase cadence over twenty-four weeks. Mobilize aligns the distributor and nominates wave-one resellers. Enable delivers bootcamps and deploys tools. Engage activates reseller-to-customer conversations using provocative hooks and structured discovery, generating qualified pipeline through deal registrations. Accelerate drives deal closure and initiates cross-sell expansion into the broader Red Hat portfolio while capturing wave-two reseller nominations.

Campaign optimization is continuous and data-driven. Weekly pipeline reviews across all cascade tiers identify which conversation starters open the most conversations, which sales plays generate the highest-quality pipeline, and which resellers are performing above or below expectations. The campaign retrospective captures field intelligence that refines the methodology for subsequent cycles, transforming wave-one learnings into wave-two improvements and establishing the campaign as a repeatable, templatable model for other products, distributors, and geographies.

Market triggers in this context are observable signals that indicate customer readiness to invest in enterprise Linux: unsupported CentOS workloads creating compliance exposure, commercial Linux renewal cycles creating competitive displacement windows, VMware exit or container adoption creating modernization opportunities, and AI infrastructure buildout requiring co-engineered GPU support and management tooling.

The addressable market is substantial. Over 10,000 free-Linux servers across MENA enterprises represent invisible pipeline that never appears in forecasts. Only one in ten of the conversations needed to surface this pipeline is happening today. The six reasons to stop running Linux for free -- security and compliance, sovereign-grade support, operational efficiency, hybrid and multi-cloud readiness, AI-ready foundation, and the hidden cost of free -- create a structured value proposition framework that can be deployed by resellers without deep product training.

By mapping market triggers to specific sales plays and conversation starters, the RHEL Campaign transforms a general awareness of the free Linux opportunity into a structured, actionable campaign scope with defined customer profiles, deal potential ranges, and measurable pipeline targets.

narratives.name: Building a Two-Tier Channel Cascade for RHEL Pipeline Multiplication
narratives.description: How the distributor channel activation model transforms a single vendor enablement investment into twenty-five or more end-customer conversations through systematic cascade design, reseller activation, and campaign operations management.

narrativeContexts.context: The distributor channel activation model represents a fundamental shift from single-tier partner engagement to a two-tier cascade where Red Hat equips the distributor and the distributor equips the reseller. This cascade creates compounding mathematics: one distributor activates five or more resellers, each reaching five or more end customers, generating twenty-five or more end-customer conversations from a single distributor activation.

The cascade model defines four tiers with distinct roles. Red Hat provides enablement, MDF, incentives, and co-sell Solution Architect support (Enable+Equip). The distributor runs the campaign across their reseller base and owns program operations (Activate+Manage). Resellers carry the conversation into end-customer accounts using conversation starters, discovery questions, and sales plays (Engage+Qualify). End customers move from free Linux today to RHEL tomorrow to platform expansion (Convert+Expand). Each tier has specific handoff deliverables and attribution responsibilities.

The three-pillar support structure ensures that capability building (enablement), demand creation (marketing), and economic motivation (incentives) operate simultaneously. The half-day RHEL sales bootcamp equips resellers with conversation capability rather than product knowledge. Co-branded campaign assets and MDF-funded events extend reach beyond direct conversations. Deal registration rebates and co-sell SA engagement address the economic barrier that prevents resellers from investing in new product conversations. The target of 20 partners activated, generating $3M in deal registrations across the cascade, demonstrates the multiplication mathematics at the core of the model.

The cascade activation model succeeds when all tiers are operating independently within their defined roles, with pipeline flowing from reseller conversations through distributor operations to Red Hat co-sell engagement. The model's scalability is proven when wave-two resellers can be onboarded faster and more effectively than wave one, and when the cascade template can be replicated across additional distributors, geographies, and product lines.

narratives.name: Signal-Matched Sales Plays and Provocation-Based Conversation Methodology
narratives.description: How four sales play prototypes and three evidence-backed conversation starters create a repeatable demand generation framework that enables resellers to open and qualify RHEL opportunities without deep product training.

narrativeContexts.context: The RHEL Sales Play methodology represents a departure from traditional product-push selling. Instead of training channel partners on RHEL architecture and configuration, the methodology equips them with provocative conversation starters that create urgency through evidence, signal-matched sales motions that guide them from conversation to qualification, and economic tools that quantify the value proposition. The fundamental insight is that resellers need a script, a calculator, a value proposition, objection handling, and a qualification framework -- not a product catalog.

Each sales play is a signal-matched motion: the seller observes a customer signal (CentOS end-of-life exposure, commercial Linux renewal cycle, modernization initiative, or legacy version support need), selects the matching play, and follows a defined execution sequence. Each play has a distinct deal potential range, execution approach, and upsell path. Overlaying the plays are three conversation starters -- Security/CVE acceleration, Post-Quantum Cryptography migration, and AI Foundation infrastructure -- that provide the provocative entry point for any conversation regardless of which play will ultimately be selected. The conversation starters lead with universal technology concerns, not product features.

The evidence base supporting the conversation starters draws from authoritative third-party sources: Mandiant M-Trends documenting negative-seven-day mean time to exploit, NIST PQC standards creating compliance mandates, and RAND Corporation research documenting eighty-percent AI project failure rates. Red Hat capabilities (Project Lightwell, RHEL 10.1 PQC, MCP integration) are positioned as responses to these evidence-backed challenges, not as feature lists. This evidence-first approach enables resellers to have credible conversations even without deep Red Hat product knowledge.

The sales play methodology's value lies in its repeatability and scalability. A reseller who has completed a half-day bootcamp can identify customer signals, select the matching play, deliver a provocative conversation starter, ask structured discovery questions, qualify the opportunity, and register a deal -- all without needing to understand RHEL internals. This conversation capability, not product knowledge, is what the campaign builds across the channel cascade.

Resellers lack the product expertise to lead with RHEL features, and traditional product-push approaches fail because customers running free Linux do not see themselves as having a problem that requires a commercial operating system.

The conversation starter kit equips resellers with provocative, evidence-backed hooks (Security/CVE acceleration, PQC migration, AI infrastructure burden) that create urgency through universal technology concerns rather than product features, enabling resellers to open credible conversations using third-party evidence and structured discovery questions that simultaneously qualify the opportunity and educate the customer about risks they may not have considered.

activities.name: Design Channel Cascade
activities.description: Define the multi-tier campaign distribution model with cascade roles, handoffs, and multiplication targets.

narratives.name: Designing a Four-Tier Channel Cascade for RHEL Pipeline
narratives.description: How the cascade design activity produces the organizational framework for multi-tier campaign distribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Distributor campaigns require defining the organizational layers between the vendor and the end customer, and the RHEL campaign identifies four tiers -- Red Hat, Distributor, Reseller, End Customer -- each with explicit roles, handoff deliverables, and attribution responsibilities that must be documented before any activation begins.

Traditional single-tier partner engagement designs do not account for the content adaptation, quality assurance, and attribution tracking challenges introduced by the second cascade layer, and the multiplication mathematics that make the model economically viable (one distributor activating five-plus resellers reaching twenty-five-plus end customers) must be grounded in the distributor's actual network size rather than aspirational targets.

The cascade design activity produces a documented four-tier model with action-oriented role labels (Enable+Equip, Activate+Manage, Engage+Qualify, Convert+Expand), specifies content adaptation requirements for each tier transition, establishes attribution tracking mechanisms spanning marketing campaign codes, deal registration, and automated pipeline reporting across organizational boundaries, and sets multiplication targets calibrated to the distributor's actual reseller base and customer reach.

activities.name: Develop Conversation Starters
activities.description: Create provocative evidence-backed hooks with discovery questions and supporting evidence for opening RHEL conversations.

narratives.name: Creating Provocative Hooks That Open Doors Without Pushing Products
narratives.description: How evidence-backed conversation starters are designed to open customer conversations through provocation rather than product push.

narrativeContexts.context: Effective demand generation for enterprise Linux requires conversation starters that transcend specific customer technologies, and the three hooks in this campaign -- Security/CVE acceleration, Post-Quantum Cryptography expiration, and AI infrastructure management burden -- address universal concerns relevant to any enterprise with Linux workloads.

Traditional product marketing fails because it leads with features that customers running free Linux do not believe they need, and resellers lack the product expertise to credibly present technical capabilities. The hook must create urgency without mentioning the product and must be supported by credible third-party evidence rather than vendor claims.

Each conversation starter is developed with a provocative statement designed to be memorable and slightly uncomfortable, supported by third-party research citations (Mandiant, NIST, RAND Corporation), structured with discovery questions that simultaneously advance the conversation and qualify the opportunity, and produced in two variants -- partner-facing for resellers with customer-engagement focus and seller-facing for Red Hat sellers with additional internal actions for opportunity tagging and services attachment.

activities.name: Define Sales Play Prototypes
activities.description: Design signal-matched sales motions with customer profiles, execution steps, deal potential ranges, and upsell paths.

narratives.name: Designing Signal-Matched Sales Motions for RHEL Conversion
narratives.description: How four signal-matched sales play prototypes give resellers a decision framework for each customer situation.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers exhibit distinct signals indicating their readiness to purchase RHEL -- unsupported CentOS installations creating security exposure, commercial Linux renewal cycles creating competitive windows, modernization initiatives creating platform opportunities, and legacy RHEL versions requiring extended support -- and each signal type maps to a different deal potential range and execution approach.

Without a structured framework for matching signals to motions, resellers default to a single sales approach regardless of customer situation, missing the opportunity to calibrate their engagement to the customer's specific readiness signal and deal potential.

Four sales play prototypes are defined -- CentOS Stranded ($3K-$15K ARR, high-volume fast close), Commercial Linux Renewer ($10K-$50K ARR, margin play), Modernization Buyer ($15K-$100K+ ARR, strategic expansion), and Extend Support ($5K-$100K ARR, multi-year) -- each with observable entry signals, repeatable execution steps, deal potential ranges, upsell paths to the broader Red Hat portfolio, and topic-specific enrichment layers that customize the base play for different conversation contexts.

activities.name: Build Campaign Three-Pillar Support
activities.description: Design and resource enablement, marketing, and incentive programs for channel activation at scale.

narratives.name: Designing Simultaneous Enablement, Marketing, and Incentive Pillars
narratives.description: How three pillars of campaign support must be designed simultaneously to ensure capability, demand, and motivation are developed in concert.

narrativeContexts.context: Channel campaigns require simultaneous investment in three pillars -- enablement that builds conversation capability, marketing that creates demand through co-branded assets and events, and incentives that make the economic mathematics work for every tier of the cascade -- and these pillars must be sequenced so that enablement precedes marketing and incentives are communicated before enablement.

Investing in only one or two pillars creates imbalance: enablement without incentives means trained sellers who lack economic motivation to invest time in RHEL conversations, marketing without enablement generates demand that sellers cannot convert, and incentives without enablement create economic motivation without the capability to act on it.

The three-pillar support structure designs the Enablement pillar (RHEL sales bootcamp, conversation starter kits, TCO/ROI calculator, qualification framework), the Marketing pillar (co-branded campaign assets, MDF allocation, event planning), and the Incentives pillar (deal registration rebates, distributor incentives to partner sellers, co-sell Solution Architect engagement on every qualified opportunity) as coordinated components with explicit dependencies, budget allocation, and sequencing that ensures capability, demand, and motivation are developed in concert.

activities.name: Nominate and Onboard Resellers
activities.description: Identify, commit, and prepare top resellers for wave-one campaign participation.

narratives.name: Selecting and Committing Wave-One Resellers for Campaign Activation
narratives.description: How focused reseller nomination creates a wave-one cohort with explicit commitments and learning feedback loops.

narrativeContexts.context: The distributor identifies their top 5 resellers for wave-one participation using selection criteria that include size of existing Linux installed base, strength of customer relationships, willingness to invest seller time in RHEL training and execution, and historical campaign performance track record.

Mass enablement across a large reseller base dilutes investment and produces passive participation where resellers attend training but do not execute. The cascade model requires focused activation of a small cohort with explicit commitments to seller participation, bootcamp attendance, minimum customer conversations, and pipeline reporting.

Reseller nomination creates a focused wave-one cohort with explicit commitments: specific sellers assigned, bootcamp attendance confirmed, minimum customer conversation targets agreed, and deal registration and pipeline reporting requirements understood. The wave-one cohort serves as both an execution group and a learning cohort whose field feedback informs refinements before wave-two expansion.

activities.name: Deliver RHEL Sales Bootcamp
activities.description: Conduct half-day workshop equipping distributor and reseller sellers with RHEL conversation capability.

narratives.name: Building Conversation Capability Through Half-Day Intensive Bootcamp
narratives.description: How experiential learning builds conversation capability rather than product knowledge in a half-day workshop format.

narrativeContexts.context: The RHEL sales bootcamp is a half-day intensive workshop structured to build conversation capability rather than product knowledge, covering the market opportunity (why RHEL, why now, the hidden Linux estate), hands-on conversation starter practice with each of the three hooks and discovery questions, sales play walkthrough with signal recognition and play selection exercises, TCO/ROI calculator hands-on exercises, and qualification framework practice with simulated customer scenarios.

Traditional product training fails because it attempts to teach resellers RHEL architecture and configuration -- knowledge they do not need and will not retain. Resellers need the ability to open a conversation, qualify interest, and navigate deal progression, not to configure RHEL packages or understand kernel internals.

The bootcamp uses experiential learning with paired role-play exercises where one seller plays the customer and another delivers the conversation starter, followed by group debrief on what worked and how to adapt the conversation. The bootcamp concludes with each seller identifying three to five target accounts from their installed base for immediate engagement, creating momentum that translates training into execution within the first two weeks.

activities.name: Deploy Co-Branded Campaign Assets
activities.description: Adapt, co-brand, and launch marketing materials across distributor and reseller channels.

narratives.name: Launching Co-Branded Assets Across the Cascade for Demand Generation
narratives.description: How campaign assets are adapted for two-tier co-branding and deployed with attribution tracking.

narrativeContexts.context: Campaign asset deployment adapts Red Hat-created materials for co-branding at the distributor level with customization points for logos, contact information, and local market references, and includes email nurture sequences, social media content aligned to campaign phases, customer briefing decks, and MDF-funded event planning and execution.

The two-tier cascade adds a complexity layer that single-tier campaigns do not face: assets must be co-brandable at both the distributor and reseller levels, and the distributor's marketing team must be able to perform co-branding customization with clear brand guidelines and approval processes that do not create bottlenecks.

Asset deployment follows a structured process where Red Hat provides brand guidelines and templated assets, the distributor's marketing team performs co-branding customization, and a curated reseller marketing kit containing the most essential assets in simplified formats enables resellers to deploy materials with minimal modification. All assets have tracking codes for campaign attribution, and MDF-funded events are planned with venue logistics, target account invitation lists, and lead capture mechanisms connected to the attribution system.

activities.name: Execute Customer Discovery Sessions
activities.description: Conduct structured conversations using provocative hooks and discovery questions to identify and qualify RHEL opportunities.

narratives.name: Using Provocative Hooks to Surface Hidden Linux Pipeline
narratives.description: How provocative conversation starters and structured discovery questions surface hidden Linux workloads as qualified pipeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Customer discovery sessions are the primary demand generation mechanism in the cascade model, where a reseller seller uses one or more conversation starters to open a meeting with an existing customer and then guides the conversation through structured discovery questions to assess the customer's Linux environment, security posture, compliance requirements, and modernization plans.

Customers running free Linux do not see themselves as having a problem, and resellers lack the technical depth to credibly present RHEL features, creating a barrier where neither party is motivated to engage in a product-led conversation about enterprise Linux.

The discovery session begins with a provocative hook selected based on customer context (Security for regulated industries, PQC for compliance-driven buyers, AI Foundation for organizations with public AI ambitions), transitions to diagnostic discovery questions that reveal the customer's current state without requiring the seller to have deep technical knowledge, and culminates in signal detection that maps customer responses to one of the four sales plays, with the session goal being qualification and next-step scheduling rather than deal closure.

activities.name: Qualify and Register Deals
activities.description: Apply qualification criteria to discovery outputs and submit deal registrations for protected pipeline.

narratives.name: Converting Discovery Insights into Protected Pipeline Through Deal Registration
narratives.description: How structured qualification and deal registration convert discovery session insights into protected pipeline with cascade attribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Deal qualification follows discovery sessions and applies structured criteria to assess whether an opportunity has genuine need (free Linux workloads, security gaps, compliance requirements), budget authority, timeline for action (renewal cycle, compliance deadline, project milestone), and deal potential within the calibrated range for the identified sales play type.

Complexity in the deal registration process leads to underreporting and destroys attribution accuracy, and without protected margin from deal registration, resellers who invest time in identifying and qualifying opportunities risk losing economic benefit to competitors or Red Hat's direct sales team.

The deal registration process provides protected margin on registered RHEL opportunities through a deliberately simple registration mechanism, with next steps determined by deal complexity: high-volume fast-close plays (CentOS Stranded at $3K-$15K) progress through the reseller's standard process, while strategic plays (Modernization at $15K-$150K+) trigger Red Hat Solution Architect co-sell engagement. All outcomes are reported to the distributor campaign manager for pipeline tracking and weekly review.

activities.name: Conduct Co-Sell Engagement
activities.description: Partner Red Hat Solution Architects with reseller sellers on qualified opportunities for technical selling support.

narratives.name: Partnering Solution Architects with Resellers for Technical Credibility
narratives.description: How Red Hat Solution Architect engagement provides technical depth on qualified opportunities through the co-sell model.

narrativeContexts.context: Co-sell engagement activates when a reseller has qualified an opportunity meeting SA engagement criteria -- typically deals above a threshold ARR, complex technical scenarios involving modernization or AI infrastructure, or situations where the customer requires technical credibility beyond the reseller's capability -- following a structured process from deal briefing through joint customer meeting to documented findings and next steps.

SA capacity must be managed to prevent overload, since with a target of 100 deals qualified for DEMO/POC, not every deal requires the same level of SA engagement: high-volume CentOS migration deals may need minimal SA touch while strategic modernization deals need sustained SA partnership over multiple engagements.

The co-sell model provides Red Hat Solution Architect engagement on qualified opportunities with structured engagement following deal briefing, customer engagement planning, joint customer meetings (reseller leads relationship, SA provides technical depth), and documented findings. SA allocation is prioritized by deal size and strategic importance through agreement between distributor and Red Hat, and SAs provide topic-specific technical support for Security conversation (vulnerability management, Project Lightwell, Satellite), PQC conversation (crypto-policies framework, ML-KEM/ML-DSA), and AI Foundation conversation (MCP integration, GPU support, confidential computing).

activities.name: Conduct Pipeline Review
activities.description: Execute weekly cross-tier pipeline reviews to qualify leads, address stalls, and optimize campaign execution.

narratives.name: Cross-Tier Pipeline Reviews for Campaign Intelligence and Optimization
narratives.description: How structured cross-tier pipeline reviews at two cascade levels transform field intelligence into campaign optimization.

narrativeContexts.context: Pipeline reviews operate at two levels in the cascade model: reseller-to-distributor reviews (weekly, 30-45 minutes, focused on individual deal progression and reseller coaching) and distributor-to-Red Hat reviews (weekly or bi-weekly, 45-60 minutes, focused on aggregate campaign health and resource allocation).

Inconsistent reviews lead to information gaps, delayed interventions, and lost momentum, and without systematic capture of field intelligence, patterns that could optimize the campaign -- such as which conversation starters resonate in which verticals or which sales plays close fastest -- remain invisible.

Pipeline reviews follow a structured agenda covering new deals registered, deal progression updates, stalled deal analysis, SA engagement requests, and competitive intelligence at the reseller-distributor level, and aggregate pipeline health, reseller performance comparison, resource allocation optimization, campaign pacing assessment, and strategic decisions at the distributor-Red Hat level. Patterns that emerge across deals are captured and acted upon, making the pipeline review the primary mechanism where field intelligence becomes campaign intelligence.

activities.name: Accelerate and Expand Deals
activities.description: Drive deal closure for wave-one opportunities and initiate cross-sell and wave-two cascade expansion.

narratives.name: Closing Wave-One Deals and Initiating Portfolio and Cascade Expansion
narratives.description: How the Accelerate phase drives deal closure while simultaneously expanding product portfolio and cascade reach.

narrativeContexts.context: The Accelerate phase (weeks 16-24) shifts focus from pipeline creation to deal closure and expansion, addressing remaining customer objections, facilitating proof-of-concept demonstrations, navigating procurement processes, and positioning commercial vehicles (ESP, ESP Lite, HCS, Private Offers) to eliminate cost-competitive objections on wave-one deals.

Deal acceleration requires balancing urgency with deal quality, and expansion has two dimensions that must be managed simultaneously: product expansion (moving closed RHEL deals into Satellite, Ansible, and OpenShift opportunities) and cascade expansion (onboarding wave-two resellers with refined enablement incorporating wave-one learnings).

Deal acceleration techniques include creating urgency through limited-time incentives, leveraging customer evidence for confidence building, engaging executive sponsors to remove organizational blockers, and simplifying procurement. Wave-two onboarding incorporates which conversation starters worked best, which sales plays generated most pipeline, and which enablement adjustments improved seller performance, so that wave-two resellers benefit from a more refined campaign model without investing in the learning that wave-one resellers provided.

activities.name: Measure Campaign Performance
activities.description: Track leading and lagging KPIs, calculate pillar ROI, and produce campaign performance reports.

narratives.name: Measuring Campaign Impact Through Leading and Lagging Indicator Tracking
narratives.description: How the measurement framework produces comprehensive campaign performance analysis with pillar ROI and benchmarks for future cycles.

narrativeContexts.context: Campaign performance measurement tracks three categories: leading indicators (partners activated, workshops run, POCs qualified), lagging indicators (deal registrations, pipeline value, revenue generated), and pillar effectiveness metrics (ROI of enablement, marketing, and incentive investments) using marketing campaign codes, deal registrations, and automated pipeline/revenue reporting with a 30-day post-campaign attribution buffer.

Multi-tier attribution across the cascade is inherently complex, with pipeline that can be partner-sourced or partner-influenced, and lagging indicators that lag activity by four to eight weeks, requiring careful management of stakeholder expectations about when commercial results will materialize.

The measurement framework produces a comprehensive campaign performance report at conclusion (week 24 plus 30 days) including actual versus target KPIs, pillar ROI analysis comparing investment against pipeline contribution for each pillar, reseller performance comparison, sales play and conversation starter effectiveness analysis, and specific recommendations for future campaigns, establishing benchmarks that inform the next campaign cycle's planning and investment allocation.

activities.name: Conduct Campaign Retrospective
activities.description: Review campaign outcomes, capture learnings, and produce recommendations for future cycles.

narratives.name: Capturing Field Intelligence for Continuous Campaign Improvement
narratives.description: How structured retrospectives capture field intelligence and transform it into actionable improvements for future campaign cycles.

narrativeContexts.context: The campaign retrospective brings together stakeholders from all cascade tiers to assess what worked, what did not, and what should change, structured around four questions: what did we plan, what actually happened, what did we learn, and what should we change for future campaign cycles.

Without a structured retrospective, field intelligence remains trapped in individual experiences and is not systematically captured, and wave-two planning proceeds without the benefit of wave-one learnings about which conversation starters, sales plays, resellers, and cascade dynamics produced the best results.

The retrospective produces a comprehensive output including campaign performance summary, detailed KPI analysis, pillar ROI analysis, reseller performance analysis, conversation starter and sales play effectiveness analysis, cascade model assessment, and specific recommendations covering what to keep, change, add, and stop for the next cycle, creating the input that feeds continuous improvement across subsequent campaign iterations and potentially other product campaigns.

activities.name: Target Account Identification
activities.description: Identify and prioritize customer accounts from reseller installed base for RHEL campaign engagement.

narratives.name: Prioritizing Accounts by Signal Strength and Deal Potential
narratives.description: How systematic account prioritization ensures highest-return opportunities receive first engagement from limited seller capacity.

narrativeContexts.context: Target account identification leverages the reseller's existing customer knowledge to build a prioritized list using a structured approach: start with the upcoming H2 renewal list, use Account Plan TDP maps for third-party Linux takeout opportunities, and prioritize regulated industries (BFSI, government, healthcare) where compliance messaging resonates most strongly.

Without systematic prioritization, resellers spread their limited seller capacity across too many accounts or default to comfortable relationships rather than highest-potential opportunities, and competitive intelligence about renewal timing, audit failures, or public AI commitments is lost.

Each identified account is assessed for current Linux distributions (mapping to specific sales plays), compliance requirements (amplifying Security and PQC conversation starters), modernization initiatives (pointing to Modernization play), and relationship strength (determining whether strategic or tactical plays are appropriate), with the resulting ranked list ensuring that the highest-return opportunities receive the first conversation starter engagements while lower-probability accounts are flagged for future campaigns.

activities.name: Pair Procurement Vehicles
activities.description: Match qualified opportunities with appropriate commercial vehicles to simplify procurement and protect value.

narratives.name: Eliminating Procurement Barriers Through Commercial Vehicle Selection
narratives.description: How matching the right commercial vehicle to each deal eliminates procurement barriers and positions RHEL competitively.

narrativeContexts.context: Even when a customer is convinced of RHEL's value, the procurement process can stall or be lost to competitors who offer simpler purchasing options, and the campaign defines specific commercial vehicles -- Enterprise Subscription Programs (ESP), ESP Lite, Hybrid Committed Spend (HCS), and Private Offers -- that simplify procurement based on deal characteristics and customer preferences.

Sellers may not be aware of all available procurement vehicles or may default to standard pricing when competitive vehicles would eliminate the price objection, particularly in cost-competitive evaluations against Oracle Linux or Ubuntu.

Vehicle selection follows the seller workflow after account targeting and before services attachment, with guidance that maps large multi-year commitments to ESP volume pricing, cloud marketplace purchasers to Private Offers, small initial deployments to ESP Lite, and hybrid infrastructure customers to HCS, ensuring that the right commercial vehicle eliminates the procurement barrier and positions RHEL competitively.

activities.name: Attach Services
activities.description: Position assessment and deployment services to deepen customer engagement and expand RHEL deal value.

narratives.name: Deepening Engagement Through Assessment and Deployment Services
narratives.description: How services attachment layers professional services on RHEL deals to deepen engagement and expand deal value.

narrativeContexts.context: Services attachment layers professional services on top of RHEL subscription deals to deepen customer engagement and expand deal value, with two primary services: Comprehensive Enterprise Linux Assessment (CELA) for environment assessment and Secured Standard Operating Environment (SOE) for RHEL providing a hardened deployment framework.

Services attachment requires coordination between the reseller (customer relationship), distributor (potential services delivery), and Red Hat (assessment methodology and architectural expertise) to create complementary value rather than channel conflict, and many opportunities are lost when services are positioned too late in the sales cycle.

The services attachment strategy follows a specific sequence -- lead with Secured SOE for RHEL, position CELA to assess the environment, leverage partners for deployment while Services establishes architectural trust -- with CELA assessments particularly valuable for Modernization Buyer and Extend Support plays where the customer's environment is complex, often revealing more opportunity than the initial conversation identified and expanding the deal's scope and value.

activities.name: Identify RHEL Market Triggers
activities.description: Identify and document market triggers that signal customer readiness for RHEL adoption across the target geography.

narratives.name: Scanning for Technology and Market Triggers That Signal RHEL Opportunity
narratives.description: How systematic trigger identification produces the evidence base that powers campaign conversation starters.

narrativeContexts.context: Market trigger identification involves scanning for technology trends and market events that create conversion opportunities for RHEL, including CentOS end-of-life leaving servers unsupported, CVE vulnerability acceleration changing the security calculus for free Linux, post-quantum cryptography mandates creating compliance urgency, AI infrastructure demands requiring co-engineered platform foundations, and commercial Linux renewal cycles creating competitive windows.

Without systematic trigger identification, campaign planning is based on assumptions rather than evidence, and the conversation starters lack the credibility that comes from grounding hooks in documented, quantified market triggers.

Market triggers are identified and documented with quantified impact estimates (server counts, exposure percentages, compliance timelines), sourced from third-party research and validated against the target geography's specific market conditions, producing the evidence base that powers the campaign's conversation starters and validates the addressable market opportunity.

activities.name: Qualify RHEL Market Opportunity
activities.description: Validate the RHEL market opportunity against strategic fit, partner capability, and addressable scope criteria.

narratives.name: Validating the Free Linux Market Against Partner and Competitive Criteria
narratives.description: How market opportunity qualification validates that an attractive trigger translates into a viable campaign opportunity.

narrativeContexts.context: Market opportunity qualification assesses the free and community Linux installed base across the target distributor's reseller territory, evaluates the distributor's reseller base for Linux conversation capability and customer reach, and validates the opportunity against RHEL competitive positioning using the six reasons to stop running Linux for free.

An attractive market trigger does not guarantee a viable campaign opportunity, because the distributor's resellers may lack the reach or capability to address the market, the competitive landscape may favor alternative solutions, or the regulatory and compliance environment may not amplify the Security and PQC conversation starters in the target geography.

Market opportunity qualification produces a validated assessment confirming addressable market size (estimated at 10,000+ free-Linux servers), partner capability gap analysis confirming that conversation starters can bridge the knowledge gap, deal potential calibration per sales play, and regulatory environment assessment confirming conversation starter relevance, producing the validated scope that enables campaign design with credible targets.

patterns.name: RHEL Campaign Cascade Lifecycle
patterns.description: End-to-end campaign execution pattern coordinating cascade activation, sales play deployment, and pipeline generation across twenty-four weeks.

patternViews.name: Mobilize
patternViews.description: Align distributor, nominate resellers, design cascade.

narrativeContexts.context: The Mobilize phase establishes the campaign's foundation by aligning the distributor on the cascade model, nominating wave-one resellers, designing the four-tier channel structure with explicit roles and handoff points, defining four signal-matched sales plays with conversation starters, and building the three-pillar support structure of enablement, marketing, and incentives.
